children: Saudi Arabia’s shipping major Bahri has placed orders for three very large crude carriers (VLCCs) with International Maritime Industries Co. (IMI), the largest maritime yard in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region.
The order is valued at 1.69 billion Saudi riyals ($451 million), Bahri said in a statement to the Saudi stock exchange on Sunday.
IMI is a collaboration between Saudi Aramco, Bahri, South Korea’s Hyundai Heavy Industries (HHI) and the UAE’s Lamprell.

The shipyard, located within the King Salman International Complex for Maritime Industries and Services in Ras Al-Khair on Saudi Arabia’s eastern seaboard, has signed guaranteed offtake agreements worth $10 billion over 10 years with Aramco and Bahri for the delivery of 20 rigs and 52 vessels, respectively.
Each dry bulk vessel will have a deadweight capacity of 320,000 and is expected to be delivered in batches between 2029 and 2030.
Bahri will finance the deal through a combination of internal cash resources and bank facilities, the statement said.
The contract brings the total number of vessels being built in the Kingdom to nine, including six bulk carriers and three VLCCs.

The company said the agreement is part of its ongoing fleet modernisation and expansion strategy. It further supports Saudi Arabia’s ambition to build a globally competitive maritime ecosystem by localising shipbuilding capabilities and related supply chains in line with Vision 2030.

title: Saudi-listed Bahri signs contract with IMI for 3 VLCCs
